Float Type Level Switch Types and Selection Guide

A float type level switch is a point level device in which a buoyant float rises and falls with the liquid surface and operates a switch at a set level, usually through a magnet and reed switch or a mechanical linkage. It gives an ON or OFF signal for high level, low level or pump control rather than a continuous level reading.

TypeMountingSwitching methodTypical use
Side mounted (horizontal) floatFlange or thread on tank wallHinged float moves a magnet past a reed switchHigh or low level alarm at one fixed point
Top mounted vertical stem floatTank roof, stem hangs into liquidFloat with magnet slides on a stem containing reed switchesOne or more set points in clean liquids
Cable suspended (tilt) floatHung on its cable from the topInternal switch operates when the float tiltsSump, sewage and pump start or stop
Ball float with mechanical linkageTank wall or chamberFloat arm moves a microswitch or valveSimple control in water tanks

Points to Check When Selecting One

  1. Liquid density: the float must stay buoyant at the lowest specific gravity.
  2. Process pressure and temperature: float and housing must be rated for both.
  3. Material: stainless steel or plastic as per liquid compatibility.
  4. Contact rating and type: NO or NC, and current within the switch rating.
  5. Cleanliness: sticky or solids laden liquids can jam stem and hinged floats.
